envelope.text: **The error channel is one error, not all of them.**

why:
phase-428 W6 remainder (2026-09-06) — ledgered because the correlator's return-type comparison became a VERDICT. rclrs's `Executor::spin(&mut self, SpinOptions) -> Vec<RclrsError>` RETURNS — it collects the errors its callbacks produced and hands them back. Ours (`packages/core/nros-node/src/executor/spin.rs:7077`) is `pub fn spin(&mut self, timeout: core::time::Duration) -> !`: it never returns, so there is no place to put a `Vec` and no allocator to build one with. Both halves are clause 1: `alloc` is not available on the terminal `core`/`core+alloc` targets (ARCHITECTURE §2), and an RTOS entry task does not return to a caller. The bound a user gets instead is per-spin error reporting on the executor rather than a collected batch; that is what makes this `adopt-bounded` and not `adopt`. The divergence is LOUD — `let errs = exec.spin(opts);` cannot compile against `-> !` plus a different parameter type.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ROW CORRECTED to the code. The paragraph above describes the RETIRED `spin(&mut self, timeout: Duration) -> !` at `spin.rs:7077`. phase-427 renamed that never-returning task body to `spin_forever` and moved the name `spin` onto what was `spin_blocking`: today `pub fn spin(&mut self, opts: SpinOptions) -> Result<(), NodeError>` (`packages/core/nros-node/src/executor/spin.rs`, by name). So it DOES return and takes upstream's argument; the correlator's return-type note is `Vec<RclrsError>` -> `Result<(), NodeError>`. The bound that keeps it ADOPT-BOUNDED is the error channel: the FIRST failing callback's error, not all of them (no allocator for a `Vec`), plus the poll-interval quantum on every exit condition. Both are stated in its doc comment, which is the envelope. Still LOUD: a ported `.first_error()?` does not type-check against `Result`.
